title: The Last Oath Again
premise: Wendell Eastwick, exiled for a storm she never meant to call, has hidden her magic for three years in Greyhallow, a city where charms are contraband and prayers go unanswered. When the old gods suddenly begin answering again — violently — Wendell discovers the surge is no miracle: the god Veyra has bound herself to King Aldric's crown and is feeding on the kingdom's devotion to rebuild her power. To free him, Wendell must reforge the broken oath-stone that once separated gods from mortals, an act that demands a storm-caller's full strength and will cost her either her magic or her life. In the end, Wendell chooses exile a second time — willingly — unbinding the king and banishing Veyra, but finding that the family she built in Greyhallow refuses to let her go alone.
about_author: Felix Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath rituals before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose loyalties cost them something, and live quietly with two cats and an unreasonable number of maps.

chapters.title: Charms for the Godless
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. We meet her selling luck-knots in Greyhallow's night market, hiding her storm-gift beneath iron rings, and caring for her found-family: innkeeper Bess and the orphan Tally. A desperate mother begs Wendell to heal her son; Wendell refuses, terrified of exposure. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety — belonging kept at arm's length.

chapters.title: The Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The sick boy is healed overnight by nothing Wendell did — a prayer answered for the first time in a century. Across the city, shrines hum with returning power. Wendell feels her own magic stirring like a tide answering a moon. Emotional beat: dread and longing tangled together; the past knocking at the door.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Captain Ilsa Vane, the king's oath-guard. Ilsa witnesses King Aldric speaking in a voice not his own, granting decrees that drain the city's vitality into the palace. She begins secretly investigating. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt as loyalty meets horror.

chapters.title: Iron Rings Broken
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The god-surge tears through Greyhallow; Wendell is forced to use her storm-calling publicly to save Tally from a collapsing shrine, exposing herself. Ilsa arrests her — but instead of execution, offers a bargain: help unbind the king, earn pardon. Emotional beat: the old fear of exposure replaced by the strange relief of being seen.

chapters.title: The Oath-Stone
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV, with Wendell present. In the palace archives they learn of the oath-stone that once divided divine and mortal authority, shattered by the first king — Aldric's ancestor — to seize power. Veyra has spent centuries mending it from the inside. Emotional beat: history as indictment; the corruption of power shown across generations.

chapters.title: A Kingdom That Prays
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Traveling to the stone's resting place, Wendell sees villages emptied by devotion — worshippers giving their years to Veyra willingly, blissful and hollow. She confronts the seduction of surrender: part of her envies them. Emotional beat: temptation; love against duty as Wendell clings to Tally's letters to stay herself.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa reaches Aldric's mind through the old guard-oath and finds the man still alive inside, drowning. He begs her not to save him if it costs the kingdom — but Ilsa refuses to choose between duty and love, revealing she has loved him for years. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit and costly.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Stone
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the shattered oath-stone, Veyra offers Wendell everything she lost: home, pardon, her storm unchecked. Wendell nearly accepts — then hears Tally's voice in memory and calls the storm anyway, beginning the reforging as Veyra's power crashes down on her. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; choosing imperfect belonging over perfect power.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Split POV. As Wendell pours her storm into the stone, Ilsa holds the king's body steady through the god's death-throes. Veyra is unmade; Aldric collapses, freed but broken; Wendell's magic gutters out — the price paid. Emotional beat: grief and triumph inseparable; victory that costs exactly what it promised.

chapters.title: The Last Oath Again
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV, weeks later. Magicless, Wendell expects exile — but Aldric repeals the magic laws, and Bess and Tally arrive to drag her home. She swears a new, small oath: no more hiding. Final image: rain on Greyhallow, ordinary weather, hers at last. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen freely, not granted.
